story: Kodiak, Aurora and Waabi are moving driverless Class 8 freight on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston under a Texas Department of Motor Vehicles authorization that has been enforceable since May 28th, 2026, carries no fee and no expiry, and does not ask for crash history.
notes: READ BEFORE WRITING. (1) SCHEMA. The brief asked for source_type 'journalism' and for rejected entries keyed text/why. The gate scripts/carousel/claims_check.py accepts only primary_official, primary_corporate, secondary_reported and data, and rejected entries keyed finding/reason. The Breitbart claims are therefore labelled secondary_reported. Each rejected entry carries both finding/reason and text/why. This worker has no shell, so claims_check.py --file was NOT run. The caller must run it before handing the file on. (2) HOW THINGS WERE MATCHED. robots.txt was checked on every host used: txdmv.gov, kodiak.ai, ir.aurora.tech, waabi.ai and breitbart.com (which has a ClaudeBot group with Crawl-delay 1 and no disallow) all permit the paths used. No off-limits host was touched. txdmv.gov/AVprogram was re-fetched live today and every claimed sentence came back. The exact characters were copied from the local HTML copy out/2026-09-26/tmp/src/avprogram.html, lines 1844 to 2067. The corporate pages were read only through WebFetch's text conversion, with two or three independent passes per page, and a quote was kept only where every pass agreed. Where a pass disagreed (the Waabi 80% sentence came back once with a trailing clause and once without it), the quote is cut to the part every pass shared. (3) CURLY APOSTROPHES. c28 and c33 contain an apostrophe that WebFetch reported as U+2019 (curly). That is a single model reading of a glyph, so both are marked medium. Every other quote was chosen to avoid apostrophes. (4) THE ADOPTED RULE PDF. Today's live fetch of Chap_220_Final_-_Adopt.pdf returned application/pdf, 267.6 KB, and WebFetch could not decode the text. It did see 'City of Dallas', 'February 27, 2026' and 'May 28, 2026' in the binary. WebFetch saved the binary under ~/.claude, and that copy was NOT read or copied. c18 to c21 were matched against the extraction out/2026-09-26/tmp/src/chap_220_final_-_adopt_81daad35.txt, with margin line numbers dropped and line breaks joined. In c19 and c20 runs of double spaces left by the extraction were collapsed to single spaces ('submit  crash history or  proof', 'in  Government Code'). No word or symbol was changed, and '§ 545.453' keeps the space the extraction shows. These are marked medium because the live PDF text could not be re-read today. (5) DISTANCES DISAGREE AND MUST NOT BE RECONCILED. Kodiak says the Dallas–Fort Worth and Houston metros are '219 miles apart along Interstate 45' (c25). Waabi says I-45 connects the two hubs 'across roughly 240 miles' (c33). Both are company claims. Attribute each to its company, and never average, pick between or compute a difference from them. (6) THE OBSERVER. Kodiak's lane release does NOT say an observer will stay aboard until any date. It says 'the safety observer never touched the wheel' on end-to-end deliveries (c24), and it states the plan as 'unsupervised long-haul driverless service' by the end of 2026 (c22). Write 'unsupervised', not 'observer-free', and don't say the observer 'stays until' anything. (7) AURORA'S CURRENT COUNT. Aurora's own release gives the year-end allocation (200) and not a current count. The only current count, 20, comes from Breitbart relaying CNBC. CNBC returned 403 to WebFetch on both the article and its robots.txt, so CNBC itself was never read. Any use of the 20 or of the hazard-light pull-off must be framed as 'Breitbart, citing a CNBC ride' and never as CNBC's words or as Aurora's. (8) Every company figure is labelled primary_corporate. A company release is evidence of a company claim and not of a permit, an authorization or a state finding. No public record fetched here shows which companies hold a TxDMV authorization (the TxMCCS lookup was not read). (9) Kodiak's 'Dallas–Fort Worth' quote contains an en dash as printed. Keep it inside the verbatim quote only. House style keeps en dashes out of all other copy. (10) Aurora's 2030 target is 'more than 30,000' driverless trucks. The release headline says '30,000', but the body sentence carries 'more than'.

claims.text: Texas requires every company running automated vehicles commercially to hold an active TxDMV authorization from May 28th, 2026.
claims.quote: All companies operating automated vehicles commercially on or after May 28, 2026, are required to maintain an active authorization with TxDMV.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Intro section 'Automated Vehicle Authorization Requirements – Senate Bill 2807 (89R)', second paragraph, last sentence
claims.verification: Live page re-fetched 2026-09-26 and the sentence was present. Exact characters matched in local HTML copy line 1848.

claims.text: The last of the TxDMV and DPS implementing rules for the program took effect on February 27th, 2026.
claims.quote: The department and DPS both proposed and adopted administrative rules related to the new programs, the latest of which become effective on February 27, 2026.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Intro section, second paragraph, second sentence
claims.verification: Live page re-fetched. Exact match in local HTML line 1848.

claims.text: The department defines commercial activity as moving property or passengers for a commercial enterprise on Texas roads with no human driver.
claims.quote: Operation of an automated motor vehicle to transport property or passengers in furtherance of a commercial enterprise on Texas roads without a human driver.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 1939. Definitions tab present on the live fetch.

claims.text: Privately owned vehicles used for personal driving need no authorization.
claims.quote: Individually owned vehicles, operated for personal use, do not require an authorization.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Authorization tab, first paragraph, last sentence
claims.verification: Live fetch returned the identical sentence. Exact match in local HTML line 1991.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges in writing that the vehicle can operate in compliance with Texas traffic and motor vehicle laws.
claims.quote: Capable of operating in compliance with applicable traffic and motor vehicle laws of this state
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Authorization tab, item 1 of the numbered list introduced by 'The applicant must also acknowledge a written statement that the vehicle is:'
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 1996 (the trailing semicolon was left off the quote). Item present on the live fetch.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges the vehicle carries a required recording device.
claims.quote: Equipped with a required recording device
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 1997. Present on the live fetch.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges the automated driving system complies with federal law.
claims.quote: Equipped with an automated driving system in compliance with applicable federal law
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 1998. Present on the live fetch.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges the vehicle can reach a minimal risk condition if its driving system fails.
claims.quote: Capable of achieving a minimal risk condition if a failure of the automated driving system occurs that renders the system unable to perform
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 1999. The live fetch showed the first part of the item.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges the vehicle is registered and titled under Texas law.
claims.quote: Registered and titled in accordance with the laws of this state
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2000. Present on the live fetch.

claims.text: An applicant acknowledges the vehicle is insured or self-insured at least to the level state or federal law requires.
claims.quote: Covered by motor vehicle liability coverage or self-insurance in an amount equal to or greater than the amount of coverage that is required under the laws of this state or federal law
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2001. The quote stops before ', as applicable to the type and use of the vehicle.'

claims.text: An applicant also certifies that DPS has received its plan for how emergency responders should deal with the vehicle.
claims.quote: The applicant must also certify that the Texas Department of Public Safety has been provided a copy of the plan specifying how a person who provides firefighting, law enforcement, ambulance, medical, or other emergency services should interact with the automated motor vehicle during the provision of those services
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Authorization tab, paragraph after the numbered list
claims.verification: Live fetch returned it. Exact match in local HTML line 2004. The quote stops before ' as required by Texas Transportation Code, §545.455.'

claims.text: The authorization costs nothing and lasts until the department revokes it.
claims.quote: No fees are required for an authorization to operate automated vehicles. Authorizations do not expire and are valid until revoked by the department.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Live fetch returned both sentences identically. Exact match in local HTML line 2006.

claims.text: The department counts an operation as endangering the public when it has caused, or is likely to cause, serious bodily injury.
claims.quote: The operation of an automated motor vehicle is considered to endanger the public when the operation has resulted, or is likely to result, in serious bodily injury as defined by Section 1.07, Texas Penal Code.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2060. The live fetch returned the phrase.

claims.text: The department says it probably won't take administrative action on a complaint that falls below that serious-injury standard.
claims.quote: The department is unlikely to take administrative enforcement action in cases that do not meet this standard as defined by Texas Penal Code, Section 1.07.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Enforcement tab, second paragraph, last sentence
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2058.

claims.text: A holder hit with an enforcement decision gets 10 days to ask for review at the State Office of Administrative Hearings.
claims.quote: An authorization holder has 10 days to request that a final decision be reviewed by the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH).
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: Live fetch returned it identically. Exact match in local HTML line 2066.

claims.text: The department files for a SOAH hearing within 10 days of the request, and the hearing has to happen within 60 days.
claims.quote: The department will file a request for a SOAH hearing within 10 days of receiving the request, and the hearing must be held within 60 days of the request filed by the department.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Enforcement tab, numbered list item 4, second sentence
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2066. The live fetch's version was cut off after '60 days'.

claims.text: If that hearing is not held in time, the authorization is reinstated at once.
claims.quote: If the hearing is not held within the required time, then the authorization is immediately reinstated.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.location: Enforcement tab, numbered list item 4, last sentence
claims.verification: Exact match in local HTML line 2066. Not repeated back by the live summary.

claims.text: In rulemaking comments, the City of Dallas asked TxDMV to require crash history and to make approved operators public.
claims.quote: The City of Dallas encourages the department to require robust safety documentation, including crash history and proof of community stakeholder coordination, and to make information about approved operators publicly accessible.
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, adopted 43 TAC Chapter 220, Automated Motor Vehicles
claims.location: Page 11 of 24, Summary of Comments, lines 2 to 4
claims.verification: The live URL returned a 267.6 KB PDF today that WebFetch could not decode ('City of Dallas' was visible). Matched against the local extraction, lines 314 to 316, with margin numerals 2, 3 and 4 dropped and line breaks joined.

claims.text: TxDMV answered that the statute does not let it require crash history from authorization holders.
claims.quote: Transportation Code, § 545.453 and § 545.456 do not allow the department to require authorization holders to submit crash history or proof of community stakeholder coordination
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, adopted 43 TAC Chapter 220, Automated Motor Vehicles
claims.location: Page 11 of 24, Response to the City of Dallas, lines 5 to 7
claims.verification: Matched against local extraction lines 318 to 319, with margin numerals dropped. The extraction's double spaces ('submit  crash history or  proof') were collapsed to single spaces and no other character was changed. The live PDF was not decodable today.

claims.text: TxDMV said whether it publishes information about authorization holders turns on state confidentiality law rather than on the rule.
claims.quote: whether the department makes information about authorization holders publicly accessible is based on statutory confidentiality requirements in Government Code, Chapter 552
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, adopted 43 TAC Chapter 220, Automated Motor Vehicles
claims.location: Page 11 of 24, Response to the City of Dallas, lines 8 to 9
claims.verification: Matched against local extraction lines 320 to 321. The extraction's double space before 'Government' was collapsed. The live PDF was not decodable today.

claims.text: The adopted rule says Chapter 220 took effect February 27th, 2026, and compliance is due by May 28th, 2026 or 90 days after the Public Safety Commission's rules take effect, whichever is later.
claims.quote: The effective date of Chapter 220 is February 27, 2026; however, a person is not required to comply with Subchapter J of Chapter 545 of the Transportation Code, as amended by SB 2807, and Chapter 220 until the later of May 28, 2026, or the 90th day after the effective date of the rules adopted by the Public Safety Commission
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, adopted 43 TAC Chapter 220, Automated Motor Vehicles
claims.verification: Matched against local extraction lines 47 to 50 with margin numerals dropped. The same wording is repeated on page 10. WebFetch saw 'February 27, 2026' and 'May 28, 2026' in the live binary.

claims.text: Kodiak says it plans unsupervised driverless long-haul service on the Dallas-Houston lane by the end of 2026.
claims.quote: today announced its plans to launch unsupervised long-haul driverless service on the Dallas-Houston freight lane by the end of 2026.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI Names Dallas-Houston As Long-Haul Driverless Launch Lane, Consistently Completes Intervention-Free, End-to-End Deliveries (September 25, 2026)
claims.verification: Two WebFetch passes agreed. The second confirmed a hyphen in 'Dallas-Houston freight lane'. The quote starts after the '("Kodiak")' parenthetical to avoid its uncertain quote glyphs.

claims.text: Kodiak says it now regularly completes deliveries from its hub in Lancaster, Texas, to Houston without human intervention.
claims.quote: now consistently completes deliveries between its Lancaster, Texas, hub and its launch destination in Houston without human intervention
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI Names Dallas-Houston As Long-Haul Driverless Launch Lane (September 25, 2026)
claims.location: Body, sentence beginning 'Kodiak began its driverless long-haul launch program in August'
claims.verification: Two WebFetch passes returned the identical sentence.

claims.text: A Kodiak safety observer is still aboard these deliveries, and the company says the observer never touched the wheel.
claims.quote: During these end-to-end deliveries, the safety observer never touched the wheel, including on surface streets.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI Names Dallas-Houston As Long-Haul Driverless Launch Lane (September 25, 2026)
claims.location: Body, sentence after the Lancaster sentence
claims.verification: Two passes returned it identically. The page gives no date by which the observer leaves. See notes (6).

claims.text: Kodiak puts the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston metros 219 miles apart on Interstate 45.
claims.quote: first driverless long-haul lane will connect the Dallas–Fort Worth and Houston metropolitan areas, 219 miles apart along Interstate 45
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI Names Dallas-Houston As Long-Haul Driverless Launch Lane (September 25, 2026)
claims.verification: Two passes. The second confirmed an en dash in 'Dallas–Fort Worth'. The quote starts after 'Kodiak's' to avoid the apostrophe glyph.

claims.text: Kodiak says it has hauled freight between Dallas and Houston since 2019 with safety drivers in the cab.
claims.quote: Kodiak has delivered freight on the Dallas to Houston route since 2019 with safety drivers in the cab.
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI Names Dallas-Houston As Long-Haul Driverless Launch Lane (September 25, 2026)
claims.verification: Returned by one WebFetch pass only. 'Dallas to Houston' has no hyphen as returned.

claims.text: Kodiak says 35 driverless trucks were running commercially with nobody in the cab in its Permian Basin industrial deployment at the end of the second quarter.
claims.quote: the safety case the company completed for its industrial deployment in the Permian Basin, where 35 driverless trucks were operating commercially with no humans in the cab as of the end of the second quarter
claims.source_title: Kodiak AI On Track For Year-End Driverless Long-Haul Launch as Safety Case Readiness Reaches 93% (September 8, 2026)
claims.location: Body, sentence beginning 'Kodiak's long-haul safety case builds on'
claims.verification: Two passes agreed. The first returned a fragment and the second the full sentence. Corroborated by the September 25th release: 'As of June 30, 2026, the Kodiak Driver had been integrated into 35 driverless trucks owned and operated by Atlas' in the Permian Basin.

claims.text: Aurora says investor day attendees would ride its trucks with no one behind the wheel on part of its Dallas-to-Houston route.
claims.quote: Attendees will have the opportunity to ride in Aurora Driver-powered trucks, without a person behind the wheel, on a segment of Aurora’s Dallas-to-Houston commercial route.
claims.source_title: Aurora Outlines 2030 Vision to Scale to 30,000 Driverless Trucks at Analyst and Investor Day (DALLAS, September 23, 2026)
claims.verification: Three passes returned the identical sentence, with hyphens confirmed in 'Dallas-to-Houston'. The apostrophe was reported as U+2019 by one model reading, hence medium.

claims.text: Aurora says it is fully allocated to end 2026 with 200 driverless trucks in operation.
claims.quote: The company is fully allocated to exit the year with 200 driverless trucks in operation through Transport as a Service (TaaS) agreements.
claims.source_title: Aurora Outlines 2030 Vision to Scale to 30,000 Driverless Trucks at Analyst and Investor Day (September 23, 2026)
claims.verification: Two passes returned it identically. This is a target allocation, not trucks now running.

claims.text: Aurora says its driver has completed over 500,000 driverless miles since commercial launch.
claims.quote: having safely completed over 500,000 driverless miles since commercial launch
claims.source_title: Aurora Outlines 2030 Vision to Scale to 30,000 Driverless Trucks at Analyst and Investor Day (September 23, 2026)
claims.verification: Two passes. The second confirmed the figure is printed '500,000'. 'safely' is Aurora's own word.

claims.text: Aurora's 2030 target is more than 30,000 driverless trucks in operation.
claims.quote: Aurora will outline its 2030 vision, targeting more than 30,000 driverless trucks in operation
claims.source_title: Aurora Outlines 2030 Vision to Scale to 30,000 Driverless Trucks at Analyst and Investor Day (September 23, 2026)
claims.verification: Two passes returned it identically.

claims.text: Waabi says its own Dallas-Houston load volumes have grown more than 80% in 2026.
claims.quote: commercial freight operations between Dallas and Houston are scaling rapidly, with load volumes growing more than 80% in 2026 alone
claims.source_title: Waabi, 80% Growth on Long Haul's Toughest Corridor (September 15, 2026)
claims.location: Body, sentence beginning 'Waabi's commercial freight operations'
claims.verification: Three passes. The growth is in Waabi's own operations and not in all I-45 freight. The quote is trimmed to the span every pass agreed on.

claims.text: Waabi describes I-45 as the backbone of the Texas Triangle, running roughly 240 miles between two major hubs.
claims.quote: Interstate 45 (I-45) is the backbone of the Texas Triangle, connecting two of the country’s largest economic and logistics hubs across roughly 240 miles.
claims.source_title: Waabi, 80% Growth on Long Haul's Toughest Corridor (September 15, 2026)
claims.verification: Two passes returned the identical sentence. The apostrophe was reported as U+2019 by one model reading, hence medium. It conflicts with Kodiak's 219 miles in c25. See notes (5).

claims.text: Breitbart, reporting on a CNBC ride, says Aurora runs 20 driverless trucks now and wants 200 by year end.
claims.quote: Aurora runs 20 driverless trucks now and wants that fleet at 200 by the end of the year.
claims.source_title: Breitbart, Aurora Tests Autonomous Semi Truck in Texas, Aims to Replace Human Drivers, Lucas Nolan (September 23, 2026)
claims.verification: One WebFetch pass. The sentence is Breitbart's own and not directly attributed within it. The article's reporting rests on CNBC's ride (c35). CNBC itself returned 403 and was not read.

claims.text: Per Breitbart's account of the CNBC ride, the Aurora truck pulled off the highway once for under a minute to reset hazard lights that had come on unexplained.
claims.quote: The truck pulled off the highway once, for less than a minute, to reset hazard lights that had switched on for unclear reasons.
claims.source_title: Breitbart, Aurora Tests Autonomous Semi Truck in Texas, Aims to Replace Human Drivers, Lucas Nolan (September 23, 2026)
claims.location: Body, paragraph beginning 'Most of the three hours on I-45 passed without incident.'
claims.verification: One pass, returned twice in the same response. The attribution sentence reads: 'CNBC reports that Aurora Innovation arranged the ride, putting LeBeau in the cab alongside founder and CEO Chris Urmson for a route that ran along Interstate 45 between Houston and Dallas and I-20 between Fort Worth and El Paso, ending with a completed freight run in Palmer, Texas.' People rode in the cab. No one was driving.

claims.text: A concern about an automated vehicle that could result in serious bodily injury or death can be submitted to the TxDMV Enforcement Division.
claims.quote: Beginning May 28, 2026, concerns about automated vehicles operating in ways that could result in serious bodily injury or death can be submitted to the TxDMV Enforcement Division for review at https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: added by the showrunner after the fact check; exact match on the live page fetched 2026-09-26

claims.text: Law enforcement can verify a vehicle's or an operator's authorization at the same address.
claims.quote: Law enforcement officials can verify the TxDMV AV authorization status of individual vehicles or operators at https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop
claims.source_title: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program
claims.verification: added by the showrunner after the fact check; exact match on the live page fetched 2026-09-26

rejected.finding: CNBC article https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/22/aurora-autonomous-semi-ride.html as a direct source for the current driverless truck count and the hazard-light pull-off
rejected.reason: WebFetch got HTTP 403 on both the article and cnbc.com/robots.txt, so neither the page nor its crawl policy could be read. This may be a client-level refusal and not a policy (registry section 'A standing rule'), but nothing was verified at CNBC. Both facts are carried only as Breitbart's relay in c34 and c35, labelled secondary_reported.
rejected.why: HTTP 403 to WebFetch on the article and on robots.txt. Carried only via Breitbart.

rejected.finding: Kodiak's safety observer 'still riding' until the observer-free launch
rejected.reason: The September 25th release says the observer 'never touched the wheel' on end-to-end deliveries and plans 'unsupervised' service by the end of 2026. It gives no statement or date for when the observer leaves the cab. Kept only as c24 and c22 in the release's own words. Also 'observer-free' is not the release's term. It says 'unsupervised'.
rejected.why: The release says 'never touched the wheel' and 'unsupervised', with no date for the observer leaving.

rejected.finding: Load volume growth 'on I-45' (corridor-wide freight growth of more than 80%)
rejected.reason: Waabi's sentence gives the growth for 'Waabi's commercial freight operations between Dallas and Houston', its own loads, and not for I-45 freight as a whole. Kept only in that narrower form as c32.
rejected.why: The 80% is Waabi's own load volumes, not corridor-wide freight.

rejected.finding: Aurora driverless trucks in operation today, from Aurora's own September 23rd release
rejected.reason: Three passes over the release found a year-end allocation ('exit the year with 200 driverless trucks') and no current count. The only current figure (20) comes from Breitbart relaying CNBC, c34. Don't attribute 20 to Aurora's release.
rejected.text: Current Aurora count from Aurora release
rejected.why: The release gives only the year-end 200. The 20 is Breitbart's.

rejected.finding: Live-page verification of the adopted rule PDF text
rejected.reason: The PDF URL is live (application/pdf, 267.6 KB, 2026-09-26) but WebFetch could not decode its text. The binary it saved under ~/.claude was deliberately not read. c18 to c21 rest on the supplied local extraction and are marked medium, not high.
rejected.why: Live PDF not decodable by WebFetch. Matched against the local extraction only.

rejected.finding: Kodiak ARM page end-2026 wording as first returned: 'launch driverless long-haul service by the end of 2026'
rejected.reason: A later pass printed the release's first sentence as 'launch driverless long-haul commercial service by the end of 2026' and then said both strings appear, which is contradictory. That wording was not used. The end-2026 target is carried from the September 25th release instead (c22).
rejected.why: Passes disagreed on the exact string. c22 used instead.
